summary: Shams Al-Iraq (Iraq Sun) is a data-driven web platform built by Team TechnoAstralis to analyze solar energy potential and environmental trends across all 18 governorates of Iraq. Leveraging NASA solar and meteorological observations, the platform helps users determine optimal solar panel tilt angles, estimate daily and annual electricity production, and quantify real-world power losses caused by extreme heat and dust accumulation. By visualizing solar irradiance patterns and comparing fixed panels against sun-tracking systems, Shams Al-Iraq empowers households, farmers, and engineers to make informed decisions, maximize renewable energy efficiency, reduce financial losses, and decrease reliance on polluting fuel generators. The project also features a hardware-ready tracking dashboard designed to integrate live voltage readings from an ESP32 sun-tracking prototype.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:
Shams Al-Iraq is an interactive web application that transforms NASA solar radiation and meteorological datasets into actionable solar engineering insights tailored to Iraq's climate. Users can automatically detect their location (via browser geolocation) or select any of Iraq's 18 governorates, enter their monthly electricity consumption or system size, and immediately obtain:
1. Optimal Tilt Angles: Calculated using solar elevation equations (h = 90° - |φ - δ|) with seasonal adjustments (e.g., Winter ~50°, Spring/Autumn ~35°, Summer ~10°).
2. Energy Production & Efficiency Losses: Daily and annual energy output (E_day, E_year) adjusted for thermal derating (P_T = P_STC × [1 + γ × (T_cell - 25)]) and dust accumulation losses (L_s = 0.3437 × erf(0.17 × ψ^0.8473)).
3. Economic & Environmental Impact: Estimated monthly/annual financial savings and system payback period to help replace traditional fossil-fuel generators.
4. Fixed vs. Sun-Tracking Comparison: A dedicated tracker module comparing fixed panel voltage output against an active sun-tracking panel, built to stream real-time measurements from an ESP32 microcontroller.

Tools, Languages & Hardware:
- Web Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, responsive dark UI, Browser Geolocation API, and interactive data charts.
- Hosting: Netlify.
- Hardware Prototype Integration: ESP32 microcontroller with solar tracking sensors.

Benefits, Creativity & Factors Considered:
Improper tilt angles, oversized/undersized installations, extreme summer heat, and frequent dust storms cause major energy and financial losses in Iraq. Our solution combines localized mathematical modeling, satellite-based climate parameters, clear data visualization, and real-time hardware tracking in one accessible platform.
